facts.raw_span: one week of right hip pain
difficulty walking
denosumab for osteoporosis for five years
total hip arthroplasty for a left femoral neck fracture two years earlier
JOA score was 96 on the right and 76 on the left
Initial plain radiographs at an outside clinic were reportedly normal
Repeat radiographs at our hospital demonstrated an incomplete transverse fracture in the lateral cortex of the right femoral neck
Computed tomography confirmed a lateral cortical fracture without comminution
T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a high-signal bend in the same region
Bone mineral density was 0.840 g/cm2 in the lumbar spine and 0.899 g/cm2 in the right femoral neck
calcium 9.7 mg/dL
alkaline phosphatase 47 IU/L

concepts.why: The patient has a history of denosumab use for osteoporosis and presents with a lateral cortical fracture in the right femoral neck, which is consistent with an atypical femoral fracture.
The patient has a history of denosumab use for osteoporosis and has a low bone mineral density, which is consistent with osteoporosis.
The patient presents with a lateral cortical fracture in the right femoral neck, which is consistent with a femoral neck fracture.
The patient has a low bone mineral density, which is consistent with osteopenia.
The patient has a history of denosumab use, which is a risk factor for denosumab-related osteonecrosis of the jaw.

rationales.F03: Denosumab use is a known risk factor for atypical femoral fractures.
rationales.F07: The presence of an incomplete transverse fracture in the lateral cortex of the right femoral neck is highly suggestive of an atypical femoral fracture.
rationales.F08: Computed tomography confirmation of a lateral cortical fracture without comminution supports the diagnosis of an atypical femoral fracture.
rationales.F09: T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging demonstrating a high-signal bend in the same region is consistent with an atypical femoral fracture.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation of an incomplete transverse fracture in the lateral cortex of the right femoral neck, confirmed by repeat radiographs, computed tomography, and magnetic resonance imaging, strongly supports the diagnosis of atypical femoral fracture, which is a specific type of fracture that occurs in the femur.
